questions.question: Day 10 Practice (Home Maintenance & Repairs): When talking about asking for item weight price (yesterday afternoon), which sentence is grammatically correct for 'The store vendor'?

options.a: Apples kg how much cost? yesterday
options.b: Apples kg how much cost?
options.c: I am asking for item weight price right now.
options.d: How much are these organic apples per kilo?

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option D
Natural everyday English uses standard tense agreement: "How much are these organic apples per kilo?".

questions.question: Day 10 Practice (Home Maintenance & Repairs): When talking about giving street directions (right now), which sentence is grammatically correct for 'Our neighbor'?

options.c: Signal crossing left turn take.
options.d: I am giving street directions right now.

questions.explanation:

Natural everyday English uses standard tense agreement: "Take a left turn after crossing the traffic signal.".

questions.question: Day 10 Vocabulary (Home Maintenance & Repairs): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'iron out'?

options.a: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.
options.b: Resolve minor problems or details in a plan.
options.c: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.
options.d: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
'iron out' means: resolve minor problems or details in a plan. Example: "We need one final sync to iron out contract details."

questions.question: Day 10 Vocabulary (Home Maintenance & Repairs): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'call off'?

options.a: Cancel a planned event or meeting.
options.b: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.
options.c: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.
options.d: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option A
'call off' means: cancel a planned event or meeting. Example: "They had to call off the afternoon presentation."

questions.question:
Day 10 Translation Scenario 1 (Home Maintenance & Repairs):

Telugu: "నాకు కొంచెం తలనొప్పిగా ఉంది, ఒక గంట సేపు రెస్ట్ తీసుకుంటాను."
(Literal attempt: "To me little headache is there, take rest one hour.")

options.a: To me little headache is there, take rest one hour.
options.b: I am needing to to me little headache is there, take rest one hour.
options.c: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.d: I have a slight headache; I'm going to rest for an hour.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option D
Natural Version: "I have a slight headache; I'm going to rest for an hour."

Say 'I have a slight headache' instead of literal translations.

questions.question:
Day 10 Translation Scenario 2 (Home Maintenance & Repairs):

Telugu: "మీ ఆలోచన బాగుంది కానీ మన బడ్జెట్ దానికి అనుమతించదు."
(Literal attempt: "Your thought good but budget not allow.")

options.a: Your thought good but budget not allow.
options.b: While your proposal is insightful, our current budget constraints prevent us from adopting it.
options.c: I am needing to your thought good but budget not allow.
options.d: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
Natural Version: "While your proposal is insightful, our current budget constraints prevent us from adopting it."

Use diplomatic contrast 'While your proposal is insightful...'.

questions.question:
Day 10 Translation Scenario 3 (Home Maintenance & Repairs):

Telugu: "రేపటి మీటింగ్ 3 గంటలకు రీషెడ్యూల్ చేయవచ్చా?"
(Literal attempt: "Tomorrow meeting 3 clock reschedule possible?")

options.a: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.b: Tomorrow meeting 3 clock reschedule possible?
options.c: I am needing to tomorrow meeting 3 clock reschedule possible?
options.d: Could we reschedule tomorrow's meeting to 3:00 PM?

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option D
Natural Version: "Could we reschedule tomorrow's meeting to 3:00 PM?"

Use 'Could we reschedule...' for polite professional requests.

questions.question:
Day 10 Translation Scenario 4 (Home Maintenance & Repairs):

Telugu: "అన్నా, బస్టాండ్ దగ్గర డ్రాప్ చేయండి, ఎంత అవుతుంది?"
(Literal attempt: "Brother bus stand drop me, how much will become?")

options.a: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.b: Brother bus stand drop me, how much will become?
options.c: Please drop me off near the bus stand. How much is the fare?
options.d: I am needing to brother bus stand drop me, how much will become?

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option C
Natural Version: "Please drop me off near the bus stand. How much is the fare?"

Avoid 'how much will become' and ask 'How much is the fare?'.
